Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:10:1.hebrew: איכא דאמרי סברוה כו' - וכי אתמר לימא כתנאי, אאין מעבירין על האוכלין אתמר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:10:1.english: There are those who say, they assumed, etc. - And when "Shall we say [that it is] like [a dispute between] Tannaim?" was stated, it was stated regarding [the matter of] "one does not pass by food [without picking it up]."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:15:1.hebrew: הלכתא כריכות ברה"ר כו' - כדמוקי לה בשאין בו סימן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:15:1.english: The halakha is [that] bundles in a public area, etc. - As [the Gemara] establishes it [as referring] to [an item] in which there is no distinguishing mark.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:15:2.hebrew: ברשות היחיד אי דרך נפילה הרי אלו שלו - דליכא למימר מקום הוי סימן, דהא לא ידע היכא נפיל מיניה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:15:2.english: In a private area, if [found in] a manner of falling, these are his - For one cannot say [that] the place is a distinguishing mark, since he does not know where it fell from him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:15:3.hebrew: אי דרך הינוח נוטל ומכריז - מקום, ולא יניחם שם, שמא ימצאם עכו"ם ויטלם, ושמא שכחום הבעלים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:15:3.english: If [it is] in a manner of being placed, he takes [them] and proclaims - [He proclaims the] place [where they were found], and he should not leave them there, lest an idolater find them and take them, and perhaps the owners forgot them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:15:4.hebrew: אבל בדבר שיש בו סימן כו' - רבא לטעמיה, דאמר סימן העשוי לידרס הוי סימן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:15:4.english: But in [the case of] an item that has a distinguishing mark, etc. - Rava [follows] his own reasoning, for he said [that] a distinguishing mark that is liable to be trampled is [still considered] a distinguishing mark.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:1:1.english: That they are trampled - And it is a distinguishing mark that is liable to be trampled.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:2:1.hebrew: דמינשתפא - מתגלגל ברגלי אדם ובהמה, ואינה נמצאת במקום שנפלה תחילה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:2:1.english: Because it rolls - [It] rolls under the feet of people and animals, and is not found in the place where it first fell.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:2:2.english: That they are heavy - [They are] heavy.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:3:1.hebrew: הא של בעל הבית חייב להכריז - ואע"ג דבהדיא תני לה במתניתין, איידי דנקט לאותביה מרישא — כריכות ברשות הרבים, דאותיב מינה לרבא — נקט נמי לאותוביה לרבה מדוקי' דרישא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:3:1.english: But [those] of a homeowner, he is obligated to proclaim - Even though it explicitly teaches this in the Mishnah, since [the Gemara] began by raising an objection from the first clause — "sheaves in a public domain," from which it raised an objection against Rava — it also raised an objection against Rabbah from the inference of the first clause.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:4:1.hebrew: אין מעבירין על האוכלין - המוצא אוכלין בדרך, אין רשאי לעבור עליהם ולהניחם שם. הלכך, לא נדרסו, שמי שמצאן ראשון הגביהן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:4:1.english: One does not pass by food - One who finds food on the road is not permitted to pass by it and leave it there. Therefore, [the loaves] were not trampled, for whoever found them first picked them up.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:4:2.hebrew: אין מעבירין על האוכלין - לאו לשון דריסה הוא, אלא כמו אין מעבירין על המצות (יומא דף לג.):
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:4:2.english: One does not pass by food - It is not an expression of trampling; rather, [it is] like "one does not pass by mitzvot" (Yoma 33a).

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:4:3.hebrew: חיישי לכשפים - סבורים שמחמת כשפים הונחו לשם כדי להכשיל הדורסים עליהן. ונהי נמי דאין מגביהין אותם, מיהו לא דרסי עליהן משום כשפים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:4:3.english: [They] are concerned about sorcery - They think that [the loaves] were placed there on account of sorcery in order to cause those who step on them to stumble. And even though they do not pick them up, nevertheless they do not step on them because of sorcery.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:5:1.english: Let us say [that it is] like [a dispute of] Tannaim - [Namely,] the dispute of Rabbah and Rava.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:6:1.hebrew: הבא מאיליו - הראוי לבא מאיליו, כגון חרס, פעמים שנופל בעיגול:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:6:1.english: That comes on its own - [That is,] one that is apt to come on its own, such as a shard, [which] sometimes falls into a round [fig] cake.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:6:2.hebrew: הוי סימן - דאמרינן לשם סימן נתנו שם, ולא נפל מאליו, ודבר שיש בו סימן הוא. ואפילו הכי פליגי רבנן ואמרי הרי אלו שלו, משום דקסברי מעבירין על האוכלין, והוה ליה סימן העשוי לידרס:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:6:2.english: [It] is a distinguishing mark - For we say that he placed it there as a distinguishing mark, and it did not fall on its own, and it is an item that has a distinguishing mark. And even so, the Rabbis disagree and say "these belong to him," because they hold that [people] pass by food [without picking it up], and [thus] it is a distinguishing mark that is prone to be trampled.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:6:3.hebrew: ור"י סבר הוי סימן - ואע"פ שזה עשוי לידרס, נמי הוי סימן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:6:3.english: And Rabbi Yehuda holds [that] it is a distinguishing mark - Even though this [mark] is prone to be trampled, it is also a distinguishing mark.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:7:1.hebrew: ומעבירין על האוכלין - ואפילו הכי ככרות של בעל הבית חייב להכריז, דסימן העשוי לידרס הוי סימן. ועיגול היינו טעמא, דסימן הבא מאיליו לאו סימן הוא, ור"י סבר הוי סימן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:7:1.english: And one passes by food - And even so, [in the case of] loaves of a homeowner, he is obligated to proclaim [them], because a distinguishing mark that is prone to be trampled is a distinguishing mark. And [as for] a round cake [of pressed figs], this is the reason [the first tanna exempts it]: because a distinguishing mark that comes on its own is not a distinguishing mark, and Rabbi Yehuda holds [that] it is a distinguishing mark.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:9:1.hebrew: ורבה אמר לך כו' - והכא היינו טעמא דר"י משום דאין מעבירין על האוכלין, ות"ק הכי נמי אית ליה אין מעבירין, ומשום הכי ככרות של בעל הבית חייב להכריז. וטעמייהו בעיגול משום דסימן הבא מאיליו הוא, ור"י סבר הוי סימן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23a:9:1.english: And Rabba [could have] said to you, etc. - And here, this is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda: because one does not pass by food [without picking it up]. And the first tanna also holds [that] one does not pass by [food], and for this reason [regarding] loaves of a homeowner, he is obligated to proclaim [them]. And their dispute regarding a cake [of pressed figs] is because it is a distinguishing mark that came on its own, and Rabbi Yehuda holds [that] it is a distinguishing mark.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 23a:4:1.hebrew: אין מעבירין על האוכלין - פי': אינו רשאי לעבור מעליהן כדפירש רש"י, אלא צריך להגביהן. אבל אין לפרש ד"אין מעבירין" היינו אין דורסין עליהם, כדאמר בפרק הדר (עירובין דף סד:), דא"ל ר"ג לרבי אלעאי: "טול גלוסקא משום דאין מעבירין" — הרי משמע שצריך להגביהם! ועוד, דקאמר התם: "אבל בדורות אחרונים שפרוצות בכשפים — מעבירין", ואי "אין מעבירין" היינו אין דורסין, א"כ האי דקאמר נמי "שפרוצות בכשפים" היינו דורסים! והכא משמע דבאתרא דחיישי לכשפים אין דורסין! אלא ודאי צריך לומר כדפרישית:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 23a:4:1.english: One does not pass by food - Explanation: One is not permitted to pass over it, as Rashi explained; rather, one must pick it up. However, one should not explain that "one does not pass by" means one does not trample upon it, as it says in the chapter [entitled] Hadar (Eruvin 64b), where Rabban Gamliel said to Rabbi Ilai: "Take the loaf, because one does not pass by [food]" — thus it is implied that one must pick it up! Furthermore, it says there: "However, in later generations, which are rampant with sorcery, one passes by [it]." Now, if "one does not pass by" means one does not trample [upon it], then that which it also says, "[in later generations] that are rampant with sorcery [one passes by]," would mean they trample [upon it]! Yet here [in our Gemara] it is implied that in a place where they are concerned about sorcery, they do not trample [upon it]! Rather, one must certainly say as I have explained.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 23a:4:2.hebrew: והא איכא נכרים דלא איכפת להו - פירוש: שידרסו הנכרים קודם שיבא שם שום ישראל ויגביה. וא"ת: ולפרוך "והלא נכרים שקלי ליה"? וי"ל: דדריסה שכיח, אי לאו משום כשפים, לפי שדורסין דרך הילוכן; אבל נטילה לא שכיח, שיראים שבעל הככר רואה, שסבורים שלדעת הניחו שם. אבל קשה: דהיכי פריך שניחוש שידרסוהו נכרים קודם שיבא שם שום ישראל ויפטר מהכרזה? אדרבה, ניחוש לרוב ישראל שרואין הככר ויגביהוהו, וניחוש לחומרא לחייבו הכרזה! דהא בציבורי מעות מכריז, אע"פ שאם יראו אותם הנכרים קודם ודאי שקלי להו. ועוד, דבעי למימר דאפילו ברוב נכרים פליגי רבנן ומחייבי להכריז, ואע"ג דאיכא למיחש דלמא שקלי להו ומסתמא נתייאש. ועוד, דהוה ליה למימר דמנכרים נפול וניזיל בתר רובא — אפילו לשמואל, דאמר בממון אין הולכין אחר הרוב, היכא דליכא חזקה מודה, כדמוכח בפרק לא יחפור (ב"ב דף כג: ושם ד"ה חוץ) גבי ניפול הנמצא. אבל כל היכא דאפשר לתקן להשיב ממון לבעלים ע"י הכרזה, מתקנינן; וא"כ, מאי פריך הכא:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 23a:4:2.english: But aren’t there gentiles who do not care? - Explanation: that the gentiles will trample [the loaves] before any Jew comes there and picks [them] up. And if you ask: why not object, "Aren't gentiles going to take it?" One can answer: trampling is common — were it not for [fear of] sorcery — because they trample [it] in the course of their walking; however, taking [it] is not common, because they are afraid that the owner of the loaf is watching, for they assume that he placed it there intentionally. However, it is difficult: how can [the Gemara] ask that we should be concerned that gentiles will trample it before any Jew comes there, and [thus] he would be exempt from announcing [it]? On the contrary, let us be concerned about the majority of Jews who see the loaf and will pick it up, and let us be concerned for the stringent [possibility] to obligate him to announce [it]! For behold, regarding piles of coins, one must announce [them], even though if gentiles see them first, they will certainly take them. And furthermore, [the Gemara] wants to say that even in [a place with] a majority of gentiles, the Rabbis disagree and obligate [the finder] to announce, even though there is reason to be concerned that perhaps [the gentiles] will take them and [the owner] has presumably despaired [of recovering them]. And furthermore, [the Gemara] should have said that they fell from gentiles, and we should follow the majority — even according to Shmuel, who says that in monetary matters we do not follow the majority, where there is no presumptive status [chazakah] he agrees, as is proven in the chapter [entitled] Lo Yachpor (Bava Batra 23b, and there s.v. Chutz) regarding a found chick [that fell from its nest]. Rather, wherever it is possible to remedy [the situation] to return property to its owners through announcing, we do so; and if so, what is [the Gemara] asking here:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 23a:4:3.hebrew: והא איכא בהמה וכלבים - וא"ת: לרבא נמי יקשה והא איכא בהמה וכלבים דאכלי להו, כדאמר לעיל דאיכא שקצים ורמשים דאכלי? וי"ל דהכא מיירי בככרות גדולות, שאי אפשר שיאכלום:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 23a:4:3.english: "But aren't there beasts and dogs" - And if you say: According to Rava as well, it should be difficult — "but aren't there beasts and dogs" that eat them, as it said above that there are crawling creatures and insects that eat [them]? And one can say that here it is dealing with large loaves, which it is impossible for them to eat.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 23a:6:1.hebrew: סימן הבא מאיליו הוי סימן - פרש"י דלשם סימן נתנו שם, ולא נפל מאיליו. וקשה, דאין דרך לתת מעות בככר לסימן. אלא י"ל דאימור ידע שנפלו לו שם. ומ"ד לא הוי סימן — כיון דרגילות לבא מאיליו, מסתמא לא ידע, כיון שאין ניכר בחוץ. אבל סימני בהמה שהן מאיליהן — הוי סימן, כיון שניכר; וכן דבר שאין ניכר בחוץ, אם אין רגילות לבא מאיליו — הוי סימן:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 23a:6:1.english: A distinguishing mark that comes on its own is a distinguishing mark - Rashi explained that he placed it there as a distinguishing mark, and it did not fall on its own. And [this is] difficult, for it is not customary to put coins in a loaf as a distinguishing mark. Rather, one can say that perhaps he knew that they had fallen there. And the one who says it is not a distinguishing mark [holds that] since it is common [for it] to come on its own, presumably he does not know [about it], since it is not visible on the outside. However, distinguishing marks on an animal, which are [there] on their own, are [valid as] a distinguishing mark, since it is visible; and likewise, something that is not visible on the outside, if it is not common [for it] to come on its own, is [valid as] a distinguishing mark.
